resolution: Both variants have an undefined constant P of the same Lean type `Positivity`, constrained only by axioms, and the axioms differ: Scott's A1a, A1b, A2, A3, A4, A5 against Gödel's 1970 Ax1, Ax2a, Ax2b, Ax3, Ax4. Every result takes P as a parameter and lists exactly the axioms it uses as premises, so a result says only that those axioms about P entail its conclusion. One axiom formula is shared: Scott's A4 and Gödel's Ax2b are the same statement (STMT-SCOTT-POSITIVE-NECESSARILY-POSITIVE), each claim attributing it to its own theory's P. No statement identifies either P with Aquinas's perfection.
